newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher on LME rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end higher on LME rally.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished higher across the board on Monday, cheered by a rally on the London Metal Exchange (LME) that took the metal's price to its highest levels in 19 months, traders said.
"TOCOM prices rose on the LME, but many players are more interested in palladium futures," said a trader.
"Individual investors are more familiar with PGMs (platinum group metals). They're also puzzled why LME distant months are not keeping up with the rise in three-month prices," the trader said.
The June contract gained 2.5 yen to 205.6 yen while April was up 2.8 yen at 207.8 yen. Other contracts climbed between 1.3 and 3.2 yen. Estimated volume was 4,485 lots.
In London on Friday, benchmark three-month delivery futures surged to $1,740 a tonne, up $39 from the previous day and the highest level since November 1995, mainly due to flows of speculative money.
In Tokyo, individual speculators were more interested in the yen-based precious metals market, where both palladium and platinum futures soared by their daily limits.
